thread:
maria: Quick postmortem follow-up for the kv-cache OOM (incident 1799854289). I pulled the notes from the postmortem and sketched action items. Short summary: repeated small allocs + fragmentation + stale KV refs during compaction window caused >90% resident set blowup. Need owners, short/med/long-term mitigation, and gating for Dedicated customers.

aj: Can you drop the profiler dump and the exact commands you used to reproduce locally?

maria: Sure — here is the profiling command I ran on the staging replica:

```bash
# capture jemalloc stats + heap profile
JEMALLOC_CONF=stats_print:true,metadata_thp:disabled 
./bin/runtime --profile-heap /tmp/heap.prof &
pprof --text /usr/bin/python /tmp/heap.prof | head -n 80
```

The initial histogram shows a lot of ~5-15KB transient allocations pinned in arena_2. Full dump attached to INF ticket.

aj: Ok ran the profile on a canary. I see repeated allocations from shard_indexer and the compaction path (kv_compact()). Suspect we keep small objects alive via the KV reference table. I'll add a GC sweep after compaction to free tombstones. Short mitigation: forced slab reclamation after compaction + reduce in-memory table size to 60% for 24h.

sam: For rollout safety: propose two-step plan
- short (hours): soft-limit reduce to 60%, immediate GC sweep after compaction, enable jemalloc background purge
- medium (days): add instrumentation to track live-ref counts per-shard and automated alarm at 75% RSS
- long (weeks): refactor compact path to avoid transient cross-shard references and add generational free lists
I can draft the runbook snippets for short mitigation.

rachel: I'll own the profiling and the instrumentation. ETA: EOD Thursday (3 business days). My tasks: collect 3 heap profiles across different loads, add p50/p95 resident metrics to the runtime dashboard, and add the per-shard live-ref metric.

luca: I'll own the canary and GC testing. Need a staging slot and one Dedicated customer replica for capacity tests. Tentative ETA: Tuesday next week for staged rollout. Will coordinate schedule with infra.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-2479: "kv-cache-oom: forced-reclaim-and-metrics" assigned to aj, rachel, luca. Priority: high. Links: https://redwood.internal/inf/INF-2479

deploy-bot: rollback invoked to runtime v1.4.1 on service/kv-core (reason: postmortem mitigations incomplete) — started at 1799854405

maria: To keep ownership clear, copying the action items with owners + tentative dates: 
- AJ: implement forced slab reclaim after compaction + config toggle (short) — ETA: 48h
- Rachel: profiling + add per-shard live-ref metric + dashboards (medium) — ETA: EOD Thu
- Luca: staging canary + load test of reduced soft-limit (short -> canary) — ETA: Tue
- Sam: runbook + alarm thresholds + rollback playbook (short) — ETA: 24h
- All: postmortem 1-week sync to validate trends + decide long-term refactor (recurring) — schedule Thu next week

aj: I pushed a PR for the forced reclaim flag, need review from eng-runtime. Also adding a small unit test to simulate repeated small allocs. PR: https://git.redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/922

sam: I'll add the alarm and canary checklist to the runbook. Quick note: make the alarm trigger a soft-scale down (not hard kill) to avoid cascading failures.

rachel: Uploaded the three heap profiles to the ticket and added the Grafana panels for per-shard live-ref. Panels use metric: runtime.kv.live_refs_count{shard=*}. Please validate visuals.

luca: Staging slot confirmed for tomorrow 10:30 PT. Will run the soft-limit test and post logs.

maria: Thanks — please add status updates to INF-2479 and ping me if anything blocks. We'll reconvene at weekly postmortem sync next Thursday. :thumbsup:

aj: quick question — do we want a short-term config toggle exposed to Dedicated customers? that affects SLA wording.

sam: Yes, expose it but default disabled for Dedicated. If a customer opts in they accept transient GC pauses. We'll document in Dedicated KB.

maria: Good call. I'll loop in solutions and account execs after we validate canary.

rachel: one more note: fragmentation seems worse on older kernels. adding kernel version to the heap profile metadata in the ticket.

infra-bot: INF-2479 updated: labels: postmortem-followup, priority/high, owner_set.

maria: Closing loop here for now — action owners listed above. If anything changes update INF-2479. We'll post a short summary to the all-hands channel after the one-week sync.
